composing_text: 71st Infantry Brigade; 158th Infantry Brigade; 160th Infantry Brigade
notes: Arrival in Normandy 27 June per Wikipedia list (landing beach not given). Fighting in July.

current_activity: Preliminary attacks: captures Cahier and holds it with difficulty against heavy counter-attacks
notes: Event date: 15-17 July 1944 (night of the 15th to the 17th) (Ellis, vol. I, p. 334). Event definition: In the fighting before Goodwood the division, on the right of the 15th Division in XII Corps, captures Cahier, is heavily counter-attacked and only with difficulty keeps its gain. Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 334: "On their right 53rd Division captured Cahier but were heavily counter-attacked and only with difficulty maintained their gain". Location: Evrecy, Calvados (new place), standing for the Cahier area on the Evrecy road with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Evrecy, the town on the road whose approaches include Cahier; Cahier itself is not located. Location support: Ellis names Cahier but the hamlet is not in the gazetteers used; the Evrecy road it lies on is named in the same paragraph (p. 334).

current_activity: Follows the German withdrawal: by nightfall has cleared the east bank of the Orne almost as far as Grimbosq
notes: Event date: 5 August 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, p. 408). Event definition: On 5 August, meeting fewer mines and only weak infantry detachments, the division on the left of XII Corps clears the east bank of the Orne almost as far as Grimbosq by nightfall (p. 408). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 408: "By nightfall the 53rd Division (on the left) had cleared the east bank of the Orne almost as far as Grimbos". Location: Grimbosq, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Grimbosq, the limit of the advance; the page says almost as far as it. Location support: Ellis names Grimbosq as the limit of the clearing of the east bank (p. 408).

current_activity: Pheasant: takes 's-Hertogenbosch after house-to-house fighting; resistance ceases and the garrison commander surrenders
notes: Event date: 27 October 1944 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 124). Event definition: The division gains a first footing in 's-Hertogenbosch by hard fighting early on 24 October and then spends two days in house-to-house fighting and in bridging the network of waterways to capture the old fortress town; a small counter-attack on the western outskirts is beaten off on the 27th, when resistance ceases and the garrison commander surrenders (p. 124). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 124: "but the 53rd Division by hard fighting gained a first footing in s'Hertogenbosch early on the 24th"; "Two days were occupied by the 53rd Division in house-to-house fighting to capture the old fortress town of s'Hertogenbosch"; "when resistance ceased and the garrison commander surrendered". Location: 's-Hertogenbosch, Noord-Brabant (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the town centre of 's-Hertogenbosch; the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names 's-Hertogenbosch as the town the division captured (p. 124). Context: Flagged addition: a 1944 row added in British Batch 2 only so that the new OP-PHEASANT has a British claim (Wikipedia, R672, for the name and dates).

current_activity: Ardennes: with the 33rd Armoured Brigade clears the area south-east of Marche and takes Grimbiemont; relieved on the 8th
notes: Event date: 3 January 1945 (the capture of Grimbiemont is before the relief on the 8th; the day is not given) (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 190, 191). Event definition: In the XXX Corps attack that begins on 3 January, on the left, the division and the 33rd Armoured Brigade, despite enemy counter-attacks, clear the area south-east from Marche and capture Grimbiemont, where they are relieved on the 8th by the 51st Division; the page does not give the day of the capture of Grimbiemont (pp. 190-191). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, pp. 190-191: "On the left the 53rd Division and the 33rd Armoured Brigade, despite enemy counter-attacks, cleared the area south-east from Marche and captured Grimbiemont, where they were relieved on the 8th by the 51st Division". Location: Marche-en-Famenne, Luxembourg (existing place PL0210), the town from which the area was cleared south-eastwards with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is Marche-en-Famenne; Grimbiemont, the place named, is a hamlet some miles to the south-east and the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Marche as the point from which the division cleared the area south-east (p. 190).

current_activity: Veritable: takes the Brandenberg hill by 14:00; through the Siegfried defences by 02:00 on the 9th
notes: Event date: 8 February 1945 (to 14:00 and 02:00 on the 9th) (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 258, 259). Event definition: On 8 February the division has the task of making good the northern half of the Reichswald and in particular the Brandenberg and Stoppelberg features; it leads with the 71st Brigade for the Brandenberg, the ground becomes a quagmire and all vehicles except a few Churchills are bogged, but by two o'clock the infantry are on the Brandenberg hill and mopping up the German 84th Division; the 160th Brigade, starting from Groesbeek and slowed by congestion, attacks late in the day and by 02:00 on the 9th has its leading units through the Siegfried defences (pp. 258-259). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 258: "The 53rd Division had the task of making good the northern half of the Reichswald and, in particular, the Brandenberg and Stoppel- berg features"; "By two o'clock they were on the Brandenberg hill and began mopping up the not very tough troops of the German 84th Division"; p. 259: "by 2 a.m. the leading units were through the Siegfried defences and mopping up on the far side of the Kranenburg". Location: Reichswald (forest), North Rhine-Westphalia (existing place PL0698), northern half with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the centre of the Reichswald; the division fought in its northern half and its headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names the northern half of the Reichswald and the Brandenberg and Stoppelberg features as the division task (p. 258).

current_activity: Veritable: makes good progress into the northern tongue of the Reichswald; the Stoppelberg is secured in the morning
notes: Event date: 9 February 1945, during the morning (Ellis, vol. II, p. 261). Event definition: On 9 February the division makes good progress into the northern tongue of the Reichswald; the 160th Brigade attacks the Stoppelberg feature and the hill is secured during the morning, after which the brigade pushes on to the edge of the forest, whence it overlooks Materborn; the enemy has been reinforced and makes several attacks until late afternoon against the 158th Brigade, following up from south of Frasselt, which are firmly repulsed with heavy casualties and the loss of six guns (p. 261). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 261: "The 160th Brigade attacked the Stoppelberg feature, and the hill was secured during the morning"; "the 53rd Division had made good progress into the northern tongue of the Reichswald". Location: Reichswald (forest), North Rhine-Westphalia (existing place PL0698), northern part with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is the centre of the Reichswald; the Stoppelberg lies in its northern part and the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names the northern tongue of the Reichswald and the Stoppelberg (p. 261).

current_activity: Blockbuster: takes Weeze, drives through Kevelaer and meets US Ninth Army reconnaissance beyond it
notes: Event date: 3 March 1945 (Ellis, vol. II, p. 274). Event definition: By 3 March the division, on the left of the 52nd, has taken Weeze and headed down the main road through Kevelaer to link up with the United States Ninth Army; in the afternoon of the 3rd both the 52nd and 53rd Divisions meet reconnaissance elements of the Americans beyond Kevelaer, and next morning no effective German troops remain west of Geldern (p. 274). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 274: "the 53rd Division had taken Weeze and then headed down the main road through Kevelaer to link up with the United States Ninth Army"; "In the afternoon of the 3rd both the 52nd and 53rd Divisions met reconnaissance elements of the Americans beyond Kevelaer". Location: Kevelaer, North Rhine-Westphalia (new place), at the point of the junction with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Kevelaer; the junction took place beyond it, to the east, and the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Kevelaer as the town passed before the junction with the Americans (p. 274).

current_activity: Plunder: crosses the Rhine on the 26th; attacks through Hamminkeln to Dingden next day
notes: Event date: 27 March 1945 (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 293, 294, 295). Event definition: On 25 March the corps' first Bailey bridge opens; on the 26th the 53rd Division crosses the Rhine and the next day, 27 March, attacks through Hamminkeln to Dingden; meanwhile the 15th Division has made contact with XXX Corps on its left and secured a small bridgehead over the Issel north of Hamminkeln (p. 293). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, pp. 293-295: "on the 26th the 53rd Division crossed the Rhine and next day attacked through Hamminkeln to Dingden". Location: Dingden, North Rhine-Westphalia (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the village of Dingden; the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Dingden as the objective of the attack through Hamminkeln (p. 293).
